[75] ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My two hands? Did you become arrogant, or were you of the exalted?"﴾

﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My two hands"﴾ i.e., by Myself, without intermediary, like a father and a mother. ﴿Did you become arrogant﴾ i.e., pride presented itself to you, and disdain. ﴿Or were you of the exalted﴾ i.e., surpassing him in rank.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[76] ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾

﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ It means that the animal fiery spirit (al-ruh al-hayawani al-nari) is more noble than the dense bodily matter (al-madda al-kathifa al-badaniyya), and he was blind to the divine wisdom and the subtle lordly refinement that it contains, until he clung to analogy (al-qiyas) and disobeyed God, exalted is He, in the matter of prostration.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[77] ﴿He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed you are accursed."﴾

﴿He said, "Then get out of it"﴾ — that is, out of the Garden or the heaven. ﴿For indeed you are accursed﴾ — that is, expelled from mercy and from the place of honor.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[78] ﴿And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment.﴾

﴿And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment.﴾ Al-Qashani said: The accursed and the outcast (al-rajim wa al-la'in) is one who has moved far from the holy presence (al-hadrah al-qudsiyyah), which is exalted above impure matters (al-mawaddd al-rijsiyyah), by immersing himself in natural veils (al-ghawashi al-tabi'iyyah) and by being screened off by hylic existents (al-kawa'in al-hayyulaniyyah). For this reason He fixed the curse to the Day of Judgment and set its end by it, because the time of resurrection and recompense is the time when the soul is stripped of the body and its matters, and at that time its dominion over the human being no longer remains. End of quotation.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[79–83] ﴿He said, "My Lord, then give me respite until the day they are resurrected."﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are among those given respite,﴾ [Sad: 80] ﴿until the day of the appointed time."﴾ [Sad: 81] This is the Greatest Resurrection. ﴿He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all,﴾ [Sad: 82] ﴿except for Your sincere servants among them."﴾ [Sad: 83] These are the ones whom Allah has purified for Himself from among the people of special care, cleansed of the garment of mental impurities and the veils of selfhood, and whose innate nature He has refined from the admixture of the darkness of human origin.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 38, verses 85–86:

(p-5124) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[38: 85, 86] ﴿Surely I will fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together.﴾ ﴿Say: "I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend."﴾ [Sad: 86].

﴿Surely I will fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together.﴾ That is: whoever follows you in arrogance, haughtiness, refusal of the truth, and disputing in falsehood. ﴿Say: "I do not ask you any wage for it"﴾ [Sad: 86], that is, for the Qur'an or the revelation. Al-Qashani said: That is, I have no aim in this. For the sayings of the perfect one who is established in the truth are sought for their own sake, not for any worldly purpose. ﴿And I am not of those who pretend﴾ [Sad: 86]. Al-Zamakhshari said: That is, the pretenders who adorn themselves with what is not rightfully theirs. You have never known me to be a pretender or one who claims what is not with me, so that I would assume prophethood and claim the Qur'an.

Note of caution (tanbih):

In the verse there is a censure of taklif (affecting to know what one does not know). Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "O people! Whoever knows something, let him say it; and whoever does not know, let him say, 'Allah knows best.' For saying 'Allah knows best' regarding what one does not know is part of knowledge. Indeed, Allah, mighty and majestic, said to your Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say: 'I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who pretend.'﴾" [Sad: 86].

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[87, 88] ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾ ﴿and you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [Sad: 88].

﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾ means: an admonition and a reminder for them. This is like His saying: ﴿that I may warn you thereby, and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], and His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17]. ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [Sad: 88] means: at the time of the manifestation of Islam, its spread, and people entering it in multitudes, [you will know] the truth of its report and that it is the truth and the sincere word. This is among the greatest miracles of the Qur'an, because it is one of the unseen matters whose fulfillment became manifest. For the time of the announcement of it was a time of few believers and fear from the polytheists, so not long passed before God replaced their few with many, their weakness with strength, their fear with security, and their concealment with manifestness and spread. So God the Mighty spoke truly, and His noble Prophet spoke truly, and the word of God came true against the disbelievers. And praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.
